setupSteps: Choose the bar. Take an EZ bar with a firm bend; a steeper bend shifts work from the biceps toward the brachioradialis (one coaching source, snippet). A straight bar is an alternative if the wrists are comfortable.

Load light. Pick a load you can curl for 10-12 strict reps without swinging. Plate weights and bar weights vary by gym (the bar itself is often lighter than a 20 kg straight bar; not standardised, Not found as a fixed number). Fit collars or clips on both sides so the plates cannot slide.
Stand. Feet about shoulder-width, knees soft, chest tall, ribs down, shoulders down away from the ears.

Grip. Hold the bar with palms facing up and forward, hands on the angled sections about shoulder-width apart. A closer grip is said to favour the long head (AthleanX, coaching claim; no EMG test of grip width was found). The 2023 bodybuilder study placed the hands about shoulder width.
Start position. Let the bar hang in front of the thighs with the arms nearly straight, elbows beside the ribs, wrists straight.
Back-to-wall option. If you tend to swing, stand with your back lightly against a wall or pillar (Gravitus, snippet). Do not let the lower back arch off or press into the wall hard.
Check the view. For the camera, stand side-on to the phone so the shoulder, elbow, wrist and hip are all visible.

steps.title: Take the bar to the start
steps.action: Lift the bar from the rack or floor with a hip hinge, stand tall and let the arms hang with the bar near the thighs.
steps.feel: Light stretch at the front of the arm; grip steady.
steps.visualCheck: Side: upper arm vertical, elbow beside the ribs, arm nearly straight; front: both elbows the same width, bar level.

steps.title: Set the shoulders and trunk
steps.action: Shoulders down, chest tall, ribs down, hips still, knees soft.
steps.visualCheck: Side: ears over shoulders, no backward lean.

steps.title: Curl up
steps.action: Bend the elbows and raise the bar toward the shoulders; the upper arms do not move forward.
steps.feel: Front of the upper arm working.
steps.visualCheck: Side: elbows stay beside the ribs; the bar travels in a smooth arc, not swung by the hips.

steps.title: Finish at the top
steps.action: Curl until the forearms are close to vertical and the bar is near the upper chest, without lifting the elbows or shrugging.
steps.visualCheck: Side: elbow angle about 50 degrees or less (est.), shoulders still low; front: wrists straight.

steps.title: Pause
steps.breathing: Brief hold only; do not strain.
steps.visualCheck: Side: trunk upright, elbows still beside the ribs.

steps.title: Lower under control
steps.action: Slowly straighten the elbows until the arms are almost straight again, elbows still at your sides.
steps.feel: Biceps controlling the weight on the way down.
steps.visualCheck: Side: no drop or rebound at the bottom; elbows do not move back or forward.

steps.title: Reset
steps.action: Pause with the arms nearly straight and the bar near the thighs, then repeat.

steps.title: Rack the bar
steps.action: After the last rep, hinge at the hips with a flat back and lower the bar to the floor or the rack with both hands.
steps.feel: Legs and trunk doing the lowering, not the back.

commonMistakes.title: Swinging the bar with momentum
commonMistakes.text: Swinging the bar with momentum. Why: it takes work off the biceps and loads the elbow and lower back; the most cited curl error (Livestrong, BoxRox, Rep Fitness, snippets). Fix: lower the weight, pause 1 second at the top, or stand with your back near a wall.

commonMistakes.title: Using too heavy a load
commonMistakes.text: Using too heavy a load. Why: form breaks and the body takes over. Fix: reduce until every rep is strict, with a 2-3 second lowering.

commonMistakes.title: Elbows drifting forward or flaring out
commonMistakes.text: Elbows drifting forward or flaring out. Why: the front shoulder helps and the biceps get less tension. Fix: think "elbows to ribs" and keep the upper arms still.

commonMistakes.title: Leaning back at the top
commonMistakes.text: Leaning back at the top. Why: stresses the lower back, especially as fatigue builds. Fix: stand tall, ribs down, squeeze the glutes lightly, and lighten the load.

commonMistakes.title: Dropping the bar on the way down
commonMistakes.text: Dropping the bar on the way down. Why: loses half the exercise and jerks the elbow. Fix: take 2-3 seconds to lower and straighten the arms under control.

commonMistakes.title: Short range of motion
commonMistakes.text: Short range of motion. Why: the biceps get less work if the arms never straighten or the bar never rises. Fix: start almost straight and curl until the forearms are near vertical.

commonMistakes.title: Bending the wrists
commonMistakes.text: Bending the wrists. Why: strains the forearm and wrist and shifts load. Fix: keep wrists straight on the angled grips; try a slightly closer or wider grip if one hand is uncomfortable.

commonMistakes.title: Shrugging the shoulders
commonMistakes.text: Shrugging the shoulders. Why: shifts work to the upper trapezius. Fix: shoulders down and still.

commonMistakes.title: Hips thrusting forward
commonMistakes.text: Hips thrusting forward. Why: it starts the bar with the legs. Fix: keep the knees soft and still and the hips under the shoulders.

safetyNotes: Keep the load light enough to hold the elbows still. If you swing, lean or let the elbows drift, the weight is too heavy.

Elbow and wrist caution. Distal biceps tendinopathy (pain at the front of the elbow crease) can follow overuse of elbow bending and hand turning; one physiotherapy source advises going easy on curls during a flare and dropping the load a lot (snippet). The research on conservative care is thin, and one rupture study listed curls as the activity in 5 of 55 cases (9%; figures from a search summary; deadlifts 67%). A sudden cheat swing loading the tendon is a plausible risk but no source states it directly (inference). Lower the load, keep the lowering slow, use the EZ bar for wrist comfort and see a clinician if pain lasts.
High blood pressure: avoid long breath-holding; stop 2-3 reps before failure.

Barbell handling: always fit collars, load plates evenly, lift the bar from the rack or floor with a hip hinge and a flat back, do not drop the bar from a curled position, and keep the area around you clear.
Spotter: not needed for light loads; for heavy sets ask someone to stand nearby, never to pull the bar up.
Gym etiquette: re-rack the EZ bar and strip plates, wipe the bar grips, do not curl in the squat rack when others need it, do not film other members.

Note: all sources for this item were seen only as search-result summaries (pages not opened in full); many are fitness-site blogs. The angle thresholds (160 and 50 degrees for the elbow, 30 degrees for elbow drift), the lean limit (15 degrees), the 2 s minimum rep, and all sets, reps and rest values are FitPlate choices (est.), not validated. Not found: ACE, NASM, Mayo Clinic, Harvard Health or NSCA EZ-curl pages (an ACE entry was searched for and not returned; the ExRx page was seen only as a short excerpt); a BarBend EZ-curl article; an EZ-bar-specific professional-body prescription or Compendium code; a fixed EZ bar weight; an EMG study of grip width on the EZ bar; full text of the 2023 straight-versus-EZ study; a peer-reviewed wrist-comfort trial of EZ versus straight bar; a curl-specific link to distal biceps tendon injury from cheat swings; condition-specific sources for knee pain, lower back pain, shoulder problems, obesity and PCOS; the primary ACOG page.
